record.paper_title: Open Questions in High Energy Spin Physics
record.original_question: Find a measurable and complete description of quark and gluon orbital angular momentum in the nucleon. A formal decomposition writes the nucleon's helicity as contributions from quark spin ΔΣ(x,Q²), gluon spin Δg(x,Q²), quark orbital angular momentum Lq(x,Q²), and gluon orbital angular momentum Lg(x,Q²), where Lq and Lg are Bjorken-x distributions in an infinite-momentum frame. The open question is how to measure Lq(x,Q²) or Lg(x,Q²), since they do not appear in the description of deeply virtual Compton scattering, and how to access experimentally the angular-momentum components that the theory defines.

evidence.quote: Most recently it has been possible to define gauge invariant parton distributions for all the components of the nucleon's angular momentum
On the other hand, eq. (5) suffers from a significant drawback: unlike Ji’s ˆLq, we know of no way to measure either Lq(x, Q2) or Lg(x, Q2). They do not appear in the description of DVCS.
Eq. 5 summarizes all we would like to know, but we do not know how to measure what we would like.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In QCD, the longitudinal spin (helicity) of the nucleon can be decomposed, in the infinite-momentum frame and at a factorization scale Q^2, as

  1/2 = (1/2) ∫_0^1 dx ΔΣ(x,Q^2) + ∫_0^1 dx Δg(x,Q^2) + ∫_0^1 dx L_q(x,Q^2) + ∫_0^1 dx L_g(x,Q^2),

where ΔΣ(x,Q^2) is the quark helicity distribution summed over flavors, Δg(x,Q^2) is the gluon helicity distribution, and L_q(x,Q^2), L_g(x,Q^2) are gauge-invariant parton (Bjorken-x) distributions of quark and gluon orbital angular momentum, respectively, such that their integrals give the total quark and gluon orbital angular momentum contributions to the nucleon spin.

While the integrated quark total angular momentum J_q can be related (via Ji's sum rule) to the second moment of unpolarized and polarization-transfer generalized parton distributions H and E accessible through deeply virtual Compton scattering (DVCS), the x-dependent distributions L_q(x,Q^2) and L_g(x,Q^2) themselves do not appear in the DVCS amplitude.

Problem. Identify a physical, measurable observable (or a finite set of observables in a well-defined hard-scattering process) whose factorization formula determines L_q(x,Q^2) and L_g(x,Q^2) as functions of x at perturbative scales Q^2, thereby providing a complete experimental access to all four x-dependent components ΔΣ, Δg, L_q, L_g of the nucleon helicity decomposition.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem remains an active area of research and is partially solved. Theoretical progress since 2002 connects canonical OAM to Generalized Transverse Momentum Distributions (GTMDs) measurable in specific hard processes (e.g., dijet/quarkonium production at the EIC) and kinetic OAM to twist-3 GPDs accessible via longitudinal target-spin asymmetries in DVCS. However, complete experimental extraction of L_q(x,Q^2) and L_g(x,Q^2) over all x has not been achieved; future programs (JLab 12 GeV, EIC) aim to address this, and small-x behavior remains an open theoretical/experimental challenge.

status_evidence.title: Quark and Gluon Orbital Angular Momentum: Where Are We?
status_evidence.snippet: Canonical OAM linked to GTMDs; kinetic OAM linked to twist-3 GPDs; appears as azimuthal modulation in longitudinal target-spin asymmetry in DVCS.
status_evidence.claim: Theoretical connections of L_q,L_g to measurable distributions have been established but full measurement is incomplete.

status_evidence.title: Signature of the Gluon Orbital Angular Momentum
status_evidence.snippet: Proposes observable signature for gluon OAM in dijet/quarkonium production.
status_evidence.claim: New experimental proposals continue to be developed for gluon OAM.

status_evidence.title: QCD evolution of the orbital angular momentum of quarks and gluons
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses evolution and small-x extrapolation of L_q(x,Q^2) and L_g(x,Q^2).
